indicator: Heroin seized by Douane (kg and number of seizures)
bias_limitations: Single large seizures dominate the kg series; the jump in the number of seizures from 2021 points to many small consignments. Enforcement-driven; seizures at the border may include heroin in transit.

indicator: OM investigations into cocaine and heroin
drug_specific: No (cocaine and heroin together; cocaine dominates)
bias_limitations: Not separable from cocaine; the rise most likely reflects the cocaine trade.

indicator: Registered hard-drug (Opiumwet list I) offences
bias_limitations: Not heroin-specific; dominated by cocaine.

indicator: Perceived drug use / dealing nuisance in neighbourhood
bias_limitations: Not drug-specific. Street-scene heroin use is a known source of nuisance, but this series cannot attribute nuisance to heroin.

indicator: Property crime by dependent users (e.g. ISD placements of persistent offenders)
bias_limitations: The classic crime harm of heroin. No series links offenders to heroin; ISD and persistent-offender figures could serve as a proxy.

indicator: Heroin use, adults 18+ (lifetime, last year)
bias_limitations: Too rare for a population survey: last-year values are rounded to 0 or 0.1, and the marginalised users who matter most are missed. CBS does not publish heroin in its Leefstijlmonitor tables.

indicator: Opioid painkillers used (also) without prescription, adults 18+, last year
bias_limitations: Three points; self-report of non-prescribed use.

indicator: Estimated number of high-risk opioid users (street scene, incl. people on methadone)
source: Trimbos OPAAK study 2023; earlier estimate 2012 (via NDM)
bias_limitations: Two points; the NDM warns the estimates are not one-to-one comparable (method and recruitment differ). 89% of the 2023 group also used crack.

indicator: Lifetime heroin use among mbo and hbo students 16–18
bias_limitations: Three points, no recent data; not plotted.

indicator: Clients in addiction care with opioids as primary or secondary problem
bias_limitations: An ageing cohort in long-term care: falling numbers reflect mortality and ageing as much as less harm. Painkiller problems are not separately recorded; about 85–90% of institutions report.

indicator: General-hospital admissions with an opioid diagnosis (main or secondary), excl. and incl. synthetic opioids
drug_specific: Partly (opioids; 'excl. synthetic' is closer to heroin)
bias_limitations: Coding practice; the 'excl. synthetic' series still includes morphine and methadone poisonings, and early values look rounded to 5 or 10.

indicator: Share of drug incidents involving heroin/methadone
bias_limitations: No yearly series published per drug for opioids; candidate for a data request.

indicator: Drug deaths involving opioids (EUDA definition); deaths with F11 as underlying cause
bias_limitations: Of the 161 opioid deaths in 2024, 112 were 'other opioids' (painkillers such as oxycodone and morphine) and only a small part heroin or methadone; about one in three was suicide. Not a heroin series.

indicator: New HIV and hepatitis infections among people who use drugs by injection
bias_limitations: Injecting is now rare in the Netherlands; most infections date from the past.

indicator: Heroin content of samples
bias_limitations: Very few samples (114 in 2025, many collected by field workers since 2024); earlier years not comparable.

indicator: People dispensed oxycodone
bias_limitations: Medical use, not harm in itself; included because medicinal opioids make up most opioid deaths (r = .81 with opioid deaths, n = 11).

indicator: Nitazenes and other new synthetic opioids (alerts, NVIC enquiries)
bias_limitations: Early-warning signal, not a harm count.

indicator: Published court rulings mentioning heroin
example_values: Count of rulings with 'heroïne' per year (not yet computed)
bias_limitations: Only a small, non-random share of rulings is published (serious and appealed cases over-represented). Useful for roles, quantities and sentences rather than volume.
status: Blocked (data.rechtspraak.nl not on this session's network allowlist)

indicator: Poison centre (NVIC) consultations involving heroin
example_values: Not in the published top-10 tables (2020–2024)
bias_limitations: Calls by professionals and the public; depends on how often they call, and on awareness of the substance.
status: Not found (heroin/methadone not in NVIC top-10 tables)

indicator: Antenne Amsterdam: trends in use and treatment intake in Amsterdam
bias_limitations: Amsterdam only, partly qualitative, survey groups vary by year; good for early signals and validation of national series.

indicator: Google Trends search interest for drug-related terms
bias_limitations: Relative index (0–100), not counts; reflects news and curiosity as much as use; sampling noise for rare terms. Creative proxy, to use only for validation or timing.

indicator: Opioid use disorder: prevalence, DALYs, deaths (Netherlands)
bias_limitations: Heavily modelled from sparse Dutch inputs; smooth trends by construction; best for country comparison, not for year-to-year change.
status: Exists (download needs a free IHME account)

indicator: Heroin processing locations dismantled
bias_limitations: Four points from three editions; the 2023 count was revised from 10 to 13; some sites also processed cocaine.

indicator: Transports of end product intercepted (mostly cocaine and heroin)
bias_limitations: Single point; not split by drug.

indicator: ISD placements (Inrichting Stelselmatige Daders) and very active persistent offenders
drug_specific: No (many but not all dependent on hard drugs)
bias_limitations: The measure was designed for (often drug-dependent) repeat offenders; the share dependent on heroin is not registered and has fallen as the heroin cohort aged.
status: Not found publicly (no ISD counts in DJI annual report or CBS StatLine)

indicator: Clients in methadone programmes (LADIS) and people dispensed methadone (GIP)
bias_limitations: GIP counts all methadone dispensed by pharmacies (also for pain); LADIS covers 11 institutions only. Neither is a full count of substitution treatment.

indicator: Heroin-assisted treatment (medische heroïnebehandeling): units and patients
example_values: 17 units in 16 cities (2022 and 2026); no national patient count
bias_limitations: Patient numbers not published nationally; capacity 20–90 places per unit; decline through ageing and deaths.
status: Checked (one point in data frame; no patient series)

indicator: Drug consumption rooms and needle exchange
bias_limitations: Counts of facilities, not users; no national registration; needle data outdated (2018).

indicator: People with HIV in care infected through injecting drug use
example_values: 297 people in care (end 2024); recent HCV in 2 of 490 (former) PWID
bias_limitations: A stock of people in care, not new infections; the report gives no yearly series of new diagnoses by route. Injecting is now rare, so numbers are small.
status: Checked (single point in data frame; no yearly series of new diagnoses by route)

indicator: Jellinek Amsterdam intakes with opiates as referral reason
bias_limitations: Amsterdam only; overlaps with LADIS.

indicator: Injecting and substitution treatment among high-risk opioid users
example_values: About 12% inject; about 8,000 (60%) in substitution treatment
bias_limitations: Single estimate; capture–recapture assumptions.
